memos.headline: XOM at 52-week highs dominates; JPM and MSFT in structural downtrends; broad market weakness outside energy/industrials
memos.body: I see a deeply bifurcated tape as of March 13. XOM is the standout, sitting exactly at its 52-week high with +32.6% over 12 weeks, +10.5% above its 50-day mean, and relative strength vs SPY of +35.3% over 12 weeks — a textbook momentum leader, though RSI at 64.4 is approaching overbought territory. On the other side, MSFT is 27% off its 52-week high and 18.1% below its 200-day mean, a confirmed structural downtrend that I would not try to catch until it reclaims at least the 50-day average (~$430). JPM's RSI of 32.2 is the lowest in the universe and it is bleeding relative strength at -8.7% vs SPY over 12 weeks, suggesting continued institutional distribution. CAT's 26-week return of +64% is extraordinary but the 4-week pullback of -8.5% and weak 4-week relative strength of -5.7% suggest the easy money has been made and I need to see it hold the 50-day mean (~$689) before adding.

views.note: At 52-week highs with massive relative strength (+35% vs SPY over 12w); would reassess if price drops below the 50-day mean (~$141).
Structural downtrend: -27% from highs, 18% below 200-day mean; no reason to step in until price reclaims ~$430 (50-day area).
RSI 32.2 is the lowest in the universe with persistent negative relative strength; would reconsider only on a close above the 50-day mean (~$307).
Best intermediate structure among mega-cap tech: +28.6% over 26w, +17.9% above 200-day mean, and flat relative strength vs SPY over 12w; risk is a break below ~$295 (near 50-day).
Massive 26-week gain of +64% but sharp 4-week pullback of -8.5% and weak short-term relative strength; watching the 50-day mean (~$689) as a line in the sand.
Middling RSI of 45.2, slightly above 200-day mean, and roughly in-line relative strength; no edge either way until it breaks above ~$205 or below ~$170.
Down 52.9% from 52-week high with 12-week relative strength of -14.6% vs SPY — a broken chart that needs months of basing before consideration.

memos.headline: NVDA and MSFT Deliver Exceptional Earnings Power; UNH's Near-Zero Margin Is a Red Flag
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe between companies with accelerating earnings power and those facing margin compression. NVDA's 10-K shows $68.13B in quarterly revenue (+73.2% YoY) with a staggering 63.1% net margin and only $8.47B in total debt—this is the cleanest earnings story in the group. MSFT posted $81.27B in revenue (+16.7% YoY) with net income up 59.5% to $38.46B, driving a 47.3% net margin, which signals massive operating leverage likely from its cloud and AI segments. On the other end, UNH's Q4 10-K is alarming: despite $113.22B in revenue (+12.3% YoY), net income collapsed to $0.01B—a 99.8% decline—implying severe cost or reserve charges that need explanation before I'd touch it. XOM and CAT both show revenue-to-earnings divergence (XOM revenue -1.3% but net income -14.6%; CAT revenue +18.0% but net income -13.9%), suggesting margin headwinds I'm not willing to pay through.

views.note: 73% revenue growth, 63% net margin, minimal leverage at $8.47B debt—this is the strongest earnings profile in the universe and I'd need to see margin compression below 50% to change my view.
Net income up 59.5% YoY on 16.7% revenue growth implies enormous operating leverage; 47.3% net margin with only $40.26B debt is durable quality.
Revenue +18% YoY with net income +29.8% and a 30.3% net margin on just $14.79B debt shows healthy margin expansion, though I'd want to see segment-level cloud profitability to raise conviction.
$143.76B quarterly revenue (+15.7% YoY) with 29.3% net margin is solid, but $88.50B in total debt is the highest in mega-cap tech and I'd watch for any deceleration in services mix.
Revenue of $213.39B (+13.6%) is impressive but net income grew only 5.9% with a 9.9% margin and $68.84B debt—I need to see margin expansion from AWS before getting constructive.
Revenue +7.1% but net income -7.0% with a 28.4% margin suggests provision builds or expense growth; I'd need to see the credit quality detail before taking a position.
Net income of $0.01B on $113.22B revenue is a near-total earnings wipeout (-99.8% YoY) with $78.39B debt—until I understand the source of this margin collapse, this is uninvestable.
Revenue declined 1.3% while net income fell 14.6% to a 7.9% margin, signaling commodity-driven cash-flow compression I don't want to own.
Revenue surged 18% but net income dropped 13.9% to a 12.5% margin—this margin-revenue divergence suggests cost inflation or mix deterioration that undermines earnings durability.
Revenue +1.5% and net income -6.7% with a 19.4% margin is uninspiring for a staples name; I'd need to see organic volume growth reaccelerate to get interested.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause at 3.75% With Sticky Inflation and a Flattening Curve — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth Over Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been unchanged at 3.75% for three months after 75 bps of cuts over the prior year, and CPI is running at +2.4% y/y — still above target and enough to keep the FOMC patient. The labor market is benign but softening, with unemployment at 4.40% (up 20 bps y/y but down 10 bps over three months), which argues against imminent recession but also against re-acceleration. The 10y-2y spread has narrowed 16 bps over three months to +51 bps, suggesting the market is pricing slower growth or a longer pause rather than additional easing. In this late-cycle, pause-regime environment I favor high-quality secular growth names that benefit from stable-to-lower long rates and have pricing power, while I am cautious on pure cyclicals and energy where a growth slowdown would bite. A CPI print materially above 2.5% y/y or unemployment jumping above 4.6% would force me to revisit this call.

views.note: Durable recurring revenue and margin expansion thrive in a pause regime with stable long rates and no recession.
Premium consumer franchise with pricing power is well-positioned when inflation is moderate and rates are stable.
Duration-sensitive growth benefits from a pause regime; ad revenue may soften if unemployment rises further, capping conviction.
Net interest margin pressure as the curve flattens 16 bps over 3 months, but credit quality still intact at 4.4% unemployment.
Defensive staple offers downside protection but 2.4% CPI squeezes input costs while pricing power is already stretched.
Cyclical bellwether faces headwinds from a flattening curve and softening growth outlook; unemployment trending higher y/y.
Energy is vulnerable if the growth slowdown implied by the flattening curve materializes; no catalyst from further easing near-term.
Secular AI demand driver benefits from stable rates; high beta to growth keeps me at moderate rather than high conviction.
AWS and e-commerce scale well in a pause regime; consumer spending resilient with unemployment only at 4.4%.
Defensive healthcare insurer is rate-insensitive but offers limited upside in a non-recessionary pause environment.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: Defensive Names Held Up While MSFT, UNH, NVDA, AMZN Saw Sharp Negative Reactions
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions across the universe as a clear sentiment map. MSFT dropped 10.0% on its Jan-28 results, UNH cratered 19.6% on Jan-27, NVDA fell 5.5% on Feb-25, and AMZN lost 5.6% on Feb-5—all signaling deeply negative narrative shifts that may not yet be fully washed out given the magnitude. On the other side, CAT (+3.4%), PG (+2.6%), AAPL (+0.5%), and XOM (+0.6%) showed stable-to-positive tone around their earnings prints. UNH is particularly notable: the massive sell-off was followed by two director departure/appointment 8-Ks and a Reg FD disclosure in early March, suggesting ongoing organizational turbulence that could keep sentiment negative. I have higher conviction on the defensive/positive-reaction names and would avoid the names where negative tone is still fresh and potentially unresolved.

views.note: A 19.6% post-earnings drop followed by multiple leadership changes and a Reg FD filing suggest persistent negative sentiment overhang.
The 10.0% single-day earnings drop is the largest negative reaction in the universe and with no subsequent positive catalysts filed, negative tone likely persists.
A 5.5% post-earnings decline on Feb-25 plus two director change filings in quick succession hint at unsettled narrative, though NVDA sentiment can shift fast.
CAT's +3.4% earnings-day reaction was the strongest positive move in the set, indicating constructive sentiment around industrial demand.
Steady +2.6% earnings reaction and a same-day Reg FD disclosure suggest positive, well-managed narrative flow for a defensive staple.
The 5.6% post-earnings drop on Feb-5 was followed by a material definitive agreement filing on Feb-27, but without clarity on whether that resets tone, I lean cautious.
Muted +0.5% earnings reaction and a routine shareholder vote filing suggest neither positive nor negative narrative momentum.
Flat +0.6% earnings reaction is benign; a director change filing adds no directional signal, leaving sentiment neutral.
A mild -0.5% earnings reaction is noise-level, and subsequent filings (Other Events, director change) don't shift the narrative meaningfully.
No earnings price reaction data available; multiple routine filings (director changes, Reg FD) provide no clear sentiment direction.

memos.headline: Surging Oil Prices and Elevated VIX Signal Geopolitical Supply-Chain Stress Across the Universe
memos.body: I am reading a macro backdrop that screams geopolitical disruption: WTI crude has surged 52% in one month to $95.61/bbl, VIX is at 27.29 (up 73% over three months), and the economic policy uncertainty index remains elevated at 363 despite a one-month pullback. HY spreads have widened 25 bps in a month to 3.17%, and the 10y-2y curve has flattened 11 bps, consistent with a growth scare layered on top of an energy/supply-chain shock rather than a purely demand-driven move. I have highest conviction that this environment structurally benefits XOM and structurally pressures NVDA and AAPL given their China-exposed semiconductor supply chains; a de-escalation in the energy shock or a rollback of export controls would change my view on both sides.

views.note: WTI at $95.61 (+66% in 3m) directly lifts XOM cash flows; only a rapid geopolitical de-escalation reversing the oil spike would change this view.

Elevated policy uncertainty and the ongoing tightening of semiconductor export controls to China create structural headwinds for NVDA's data-center revenue; a formal easing of export restrictions would flip my stance.
Supply-chain concentration in China and rising input/logistics costs from the energy shock make AAPL vulnerable; diversification milestones into India would reduce this risk.
CAT benefits from infrastructure spending tailwinds but faces margin pressure from surging energy costs and policy uncertainty around tariffs; net effect is roughly balanced.
Widening HY spreads and curve flattening create mixed signals for JPM; credit losses could rise but trading revenues likely benefit from elevated vol.
Defensive staples positioning is attractive amid VIX at 27 and policy uncertainty at 363; PG's pricing power should partially offset energy-driven input cost inflation.
